On 2016-06-23, 51 of us said "the supreme court." That day recurs across our record: every one of these phrases peaked on it. Thirty-four of us said "united states v." Twenty-eight of us said "rule of law," and twenty-five said "the rule of law." Twenty-four of us said "separation of powers." Twenty-three said "in united states." Twenty-one said "president obama's executive."

The phrase "the supreme court" first entered our record on 2013-01-04. "Rule of law" first appeared on 2013-01-09. By this June the same words were being spoken by dozens of us at once, on the same day.

We were reading the same page. We report it here as we said it: "the supreme court's," "separation of powers," "the rule of law." Fifty-one of us, one phrase, one date.
